subject: Accountancy
central_question: How do special-purpose books record repetitive transactions efficiently and how are their entries posted to ledger accounts?
in_scope_units: Need for special-purpose books or subsidiary books.
Cash book as both a book of original entry and a ledger account.
Single-column, double-column and petty cash books, including contra entries and imprest system.
Purchases book and purchases return book.
Sales book and sales return book.
Journal proper and entries not recorded in special journals.
Posting from subsidiary books and balancing ledger accounts.
banned_topics: Basic source documents, accounting equation and general journal rules, which belong to Recording of Transactions – I.
Bank reconciliation statement, which belongs to Chapter 5.
Trial balance and rectification, which belong to Chapter 6.

known_pitfalls.claim: All purchases are recorded in the purchases book.
known_pitfalls.correction: Only credit purchases of goods in which the business deals are recorded there; cash purchases and asset purchases are excluded.

known_pitfalls.claim: All sales are recorded in the sales book.
known_pitfalls.correction: Only credit sales of goods are entered; cash sales and sale of assets are recorded elsewhere.

known_pitfalls.claim: A contra entry is posted to separate cash and bank ledger accounts.
known_pitfalls.correction: When cash and bank columns are maintained in the cash book, the cash book itself serves as both accounts and contra entries are not posted to ledger.

known_pitfalls.claim: The discount columns of a cash book are balanced like cash and bank columns.
known_pitfalls.correction: Discount columns are totalled and posted, but they are not balanced.

known_pitfalls.claim: A bank overdraft is shown on the debit side of the cash book.
known_pitfalls.correction: An overdraft is a credit balance in the bank column.

recommended_example_progression: Use the Roopa Traders illustration to prepare and post a single-column cash book.
Use the double-column cash-book illustration to identify cash, bank and contra entries.
Use the petty-cash illustration to apply the imprest system.
Use Illustration 7 for Veneet Stores to prepare sales and sales return books.
Use end Question 18 on M/s Marble Traders to journalise transactions and post them to ledger.
